OCR Document Multi-Document Search Test Optical Character Recognition Optical Character Recognition OCR converts text contained in scanned images and scanned documents into machine-readable text. OCR is useful when a PDF does not contain an accessible text layer. OCR Pipeline A typical OCR pipeline includes image acquisition, preprocessing, text recognition, text cleaning, normalization, and storage. The cleaned text can then be divided into chunks for semantic search. Enterprise Use Enterprise knowledge assistants use OCR to make scanned invoices, reports, forms, manuals, and archived documents searchable. OCR therefore connects image-based documents with downstream retrieval systems.

Enterprise AI Document Multi-Document Search Test Enterprise AI Enterprise AI systems help organizations process large collections of documents and transform unstructured information into searchable knowledge. Semantic Search Semantic search uses embeddings to represent text as vectors. A vector database can compare a query vector with stored document vectors and return the most relevant chunks. Retrieval-Augmented Generation RAG retrieves relevant document chunks before sending context to a language model. The retrieved chunks provide evidence that can be used to answer questions. Multi-Document Knowledge Base A multi-document knowledge base can contain PDFs, DOCX files, presentations, spreadsheets, and other supported sources.

Multi-Document Knowledge Base A multi-document knowledge base can contain PDFs, DOCX files, presentations, spreadsheets, and other supported sources. Their chunks can be stored in one shared vector index while metadata identifies the source document and page.
